title: Smash burgers + quick pickles
skill: Thin slicing, quick pickle, high-heat sear

notes.text: Cook 3 patties at a time in a 12-inch skillet. For more than 6, keep going in batches of 3, washing the tongs and your hands after each batch of raw beef.

move.title: Thin slices, hard sear
move.body: Thin slicing means cutting food into even slices you can almost see through. Today you'll slice cucumbers thin for quick pickles, slice onion thin for the burgers, then smash balls of beef flat in a very hot pan for burgers with crispy, browned edges.

callback.body: You've seared before: a hot pan, food laid down and left alone until a brown crust forms. Smash burgers push that idea as far as it goes. Pressing the beef flat puts every bit of it against the hot pan, so it's almost all crust.

why.title: Thin and even
why.body: Thin slices soak up pickle brine in minutes, while thick ones take days. Slices that are all the same thickness pickle at the same speed, so every one is tangy and crunchy. Go slowly: even matters more than fast.

why.title: How a quick pickle works
why.body: The brine is vinegar, water, salt, and sugar. Salt pulls some water out of the cucumber, and the sour vinegar soaks in to take its place. Warm brine soaks in faster, so the pickles are ready in about half an hour.

why.title: Why smash it
why.body: Browning only happens where meat touches the hot pan. A thick burger touches with one side. A smashed one is thin and wide, with lacy edges, so far more of it browns, and browned beef is where the big flavor is. Smash it once, right at the start, then leave it alone.

why.title: Loose balls stay juicy
why.body: Squeezing ground beef tight packs it into a dense, tough burger. Roll it gently into loose balls, just enough to hold together. They'll stay tender after the smash.

wrong.sign: The beef sticks to the spatula when you smash
wrong.fix: Press through a square of parchment paper. Peel it off once the patty is flat.

wrong.sign: The patties are gray, not brown
wrong.fix: The pan wasn't hot enough. Heat it longer before the next batch, and don't move the patties until the edges look deep brown.

wrong.sign: The patty won't come up when you flip it
wrong.fix: Push the edge of the spatula hard under the patty and scrape. The crust is stuck to the pan, and you want to bring it with you.

wrong.sign: The pickle slices are thick and uneven
wrong.fix: They'll still pickle, just slower. Leave them in the brine longer, or overnight.

quiz.q: When do you smash the burger?
choices: Once, right when it goes in the pan
quiz.explain: Smash it once at the start, then leave it alone so it can form a crust.

quiz.q: Why are quick pickles sliced thin?
choices: Thin slices soak up the brine faster
They fit in the jar better
quiz.explain: Thin slices soak up brine in minutes. Thick ones take days.

steps.text: Cut the ends off the cucumbers. Slice them into thin rounds, about as thick as a coin. Put them in the medium bowl.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front. Slide your claw back a little after each slice.

steps.text: In the saucepan, stir together the vinegar, water, sugar, and {qty:salt} salt. Warm it over medium heat, stirring, just until the sugar and salt disappear. Don't let it boil.
steps.look: Clear liquid with no grains of sugar or salt on the bottom.

steps.text: Turn off the stove. Carefully pour the warm brine over the cucumbers and press them down so they're covered. Put the bowl in the fridge.
steps.tip: Make the burgers while they pickle. Leftover pickles keep in a covered jar in the fridge for about a week.

steps.text: Cut the onion in half through the root and peel it. Lay each half flat side down and slice it as thin as you can, from end to end.
steps.look: Slices so thin you can almost see through them.

steps.text: Cut a square of parchment paper for each burger, a little bigger than your spatula. Open the buns, and put out the cheese if you're using it.
steps.tip: Getting everything ready now matters. Once the burgers start, they cook in a few minutes.

steps.text: Divide the beef into {n:burger-buns} even pieces. Roll each one gently into a loose ball and set them on the plate. Sprinkle them with {qty:black-pepper} pepper and the burgers' salt.
Wash your hands with soap, and wipe anything the raw beef or its package touched.
Heat the skillet over medium heat. Lay the buns in it, cut side down, until golden, then move them to the serving plates.
steps.tip: A toasted bun doesn't get soggy from the burger juice.

steps.text: Turn the heat up to high. Add the oil and spread it around. Let the pan get very hot.
steps.look: The oil shimmers and just starts to smoke.

steps.text: Use the tongs to set up to 3 beef balls in the pan, far apart.
Wash the tongs in hot, soapy water, and wash your hands.

Lay a parchment square on one ball. Press down hard with the flat spatula until the patty is very thin, about as thin as a cracker, then peel off the paper. Smash the others the same way. Scatter a few onion slices on each.
steps.tip: Use both hands on the spatula, and lean on it. Keep your arms out of the way of any spatter.

steps.text: Leave the patties alone while they sear.
steps.look: The edges are deep brown and lacy, and the top is turning from red to gray.

steps.text: Push the spatula hard under each patty to scrape up the crust, and flip it, onion side down. Lay a slice of cheese on top if you're using it.
steps.look: The underside is browned, and any cheese is soft and melting.

steps.text: Slide the thermometer into one patty from the side. It needs to read at least 160°F. If it doesn't, cook 30 more seconds and check again.
Move each patty to a bottom bun with the spatula.
Use the clean tongs to set the rest of the beef balls in the pan, far apart.
Put the tongs in the sink, wash your hands, and put the raw-beef plate in the sink.
Smash, sear, flip, and add cheese the same way as the first batch.
steps.tip: If the pan is smoking hard, turn the heat down a little for this batch.

steps.text: Check one patty with the thermometer. It needs to read at least 160°F. Then move them to the buns and turn off the stove.
Top each burger with pickles from the bowl, plus lettuce, ketchup, or mustard if you're using them, and the top bun.
steps.tip: Lift the pickles out with a fork and let the brine drip off first.
